rationale: Lens: scope, split and count honesty, round 6 at 8b3a5535, re-read from disk (spec.md only, +84/−39). Both round-5 asks are ADDRESSED: R4.2's residual now has a dedicated panel-edit paragraph (F2 reads untracked, agent-writable reviews/*/panel.json; deleting or rewriting a registration defeats F2 with no JSONL trace; same class as a forged exact-match reviewed_head_sha under Spec-125 item (c); F1/F3/F4 unaffected) pinned by AC-11 (ix-g) and carried into AC-18; and the estimate is 9–12 beads with the R6 split expected, in Provenance and OQ-1 with the per-requirement breakdown. The 7404845f..8b3a5535 regression check in this lens is clean: no deliverable moves between 129, the follow-on spec and 130; the one dropped exit (q9ea off the fallback arm) is dropped with a stated reason and kept where it works; the new OQ-10 is a plan-stage deferral whose either answer stays inside files already In Scope (readiness via internal/lifecycle, never a gitutil import). Round-6 question: 'any outside-tip registration refuses' cannot refuse a bead that landed through `mindspec complete` with the standard flow, because the panel gate's leg (6) (internal/panel/gate.go: `p.ReviewedHeadSHA != f.HeadSHA` → Block) pins the registration to the bead HEAD at landing and `complete` only appends commits, so the reviewed SHA is always an ancestor of the second parent and therefore of the tip — one round, complete-landed, and a fix round after the panel (re-panel bumps in place, gate re-pins) all pass, and #239 recovers through reattest for exactly that reason. The only non-forged refusal is the abandoned-registration-under-a-new-slug shape (gate leg (3) allows abandoned BEFORE staleness, so an abandoned dir can hold a rebased-away SHA); the spec chooses fail-closed there (AC-11 x-a) and names the exit, which is the honest choice given that the scan cannot order it. One minor residue: the spec's repo-convention numbers ('48 registrations at round ≥ 2 and zero -r2 directories') do not match a re-measurement on main (72 tracked panel.json, 57 at round ≥ 2, one `-r2` dir that is the non-bead `.mindspec/reviews/prerelease-r2` with a composite non-SHA reviewed_head_sha); the convention claim is true for BEAD registrations, so the sentence should say so.

Say 'zero per-round directories among BEAD registrations' and either give the measured numbers with the command used or drop the counts; the current '48 … zero -r2' is cited second-hand and does not reproduce.

findings.title: Round-6 question — F2 cannot refuse a normally landed bead; #239 still recovers
findings.detail: Normal flows, checked against the gate: internal/panel/gate.go leg (6) blocks `mindspec complete` whenever `p.ReviewedHeadSHA != f.HeadSHA` (the bead/<id> HEAD in the scan root), and `complete` only appends commits (materialization, JSONL sync, the wrapper on older binaries) before `gitutil.MergeInto`. So for (a) one review round + complete, (b) a fix round after the panel (ms-bead-fix commits on top; re-panel bumps SHA in place; the gate re-pins), and (c) release + re-claim on the surviving branch + re-panel, the registration's SHA is an ancestor of the merge's second parent, hence of the spec tip, hence of any later tip the #239 topology moves it under. F2 therefore passes and reattest accepts the #239 shape (AC-11 (i), (i-a), (i-c)); the automatic read-back then holds while F1–F5 keep holding. The only non-forged refusal: gate leg (3) allows an ABANDONED registration BEFORE the staleness check, so an abandoned directory under an old slug can retain a rebased-away SHA while the bead still lands under a new slug; F2 then fails closed on the fallback path (AC-11 (x-a)) and names the directory, round, SHA and the dependent's scoped-override exit. That is a rare, operator-visible shape (one `mindspec panel create` with a new slug after an explicit abandon), and failing closed is right because nothing in the scan can order an abandoned registration against the landed one. A fresh clone or a post-approve tree with reviews/ gone makes F2 vacuous (zero registrations) — the visibility line says so. Net: the rule does not dead-end #239 and does not refuse any bead the panel gate itself let through.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE — the repo-convention counts in R4.2 do not reproduce as written
findings.detail: R4.2 F2 'Repo convention' says 'A panel slot verified 48 registrations at round ≥ 2 and zero -r2 directories', and the consolidation admits it was not re-measured. Measured on `main` at the reviewed commit: `git ls-tree -r --name-only main | grep -c '/panel.json$'` → 72; of those 57 have `round ≥ 2`; and one directory matches `-r[0-9]+`: `.mindspec/reviews/prerelease-r2/panel.json`, a repo-level prerelease panel with `bead_id` absent and `reviewed_head_sha` = `159:a5ea5b6f,160:21181776` (a composite, not a git object id). `panel.ForBead` never returns it for a bead, so the conclusion the spec draws — bead registrations are bumped in place, so one directory holds one record — stands; the numbers and the 'zero -r2' sentence do not. Since the spec's citation rule is 'verified against the tree', the sentence should be scoped to bead registrations and carry reproducible numbers or none. Incidentally this file is a live example of why F2's wellFormedGitObjectID gate precedes any `merge-base` call.
